# Review pack: review-maintainability

Everything a worker needs for this skill, in one file: `SKILL.md`, `references/checklist.md`, the skill's other reference files and its language-neutral standards. Language-specific standards and signals are in `packs/review-maintainability.<language>.md`. Where the instructions below say to load one of these files, use its section here instead; don't open the original. Citation columns (anchors, pages, source names) are left out: cite an element by its ID in `Finding.element` and the report script fills in `standard` and `url`. `sources.md` is maintainer material and is not included.

## File: `SKILL.md`

### Review: Maintainability

Assesses how easily a new developer can understand, set up, change and extend the repository, using the local
Compliance Reviewer Maintainability Rubric.

#### Inputs

`README*`, `CONTRIBUTING*`, `CHANGELOG*`, the docs folder (including ADRs), the folder structure listing, config
templates (`.env.example`), toolchain pin files, package manifests and a few representative source files, per
`compliance-inventory`.

#### Standards (local, authoritative)

- `references/standards/maintainability-rubric.md` — MR-01…MR-36. Always load.
- Do **not** fetch any URL for this skill. Do not load `references/standards/MAINTENANCE.md`.
- If no element covers a situation: apply the closest element if it clearly fits; otherwise mark the check N/A
  ("not covered by localized standard") and add `localized-standard-gap: <description>` to `notes`.

#### Procedure

1. Load `references/checklist.md`, `references/sources.md` and the rubric.
2. For each check (MAINT-01…MAINT-10), evaluate only the elements it lists whose "Applies when" condition holds.
   If none apply, mark the check N/A with that reason.
3. Missing documents: report one only when the folder listing (or the folder where it would be) is in the file list
   and the document is absent; otherwise mark the check N/A ("documentation location not in scope"). Use confidence
   `Medium` for missing-document findings and `High` when the evidence is in a file you read.
4. Docs in sync (MAINT-09): you may open the manifest or config file a document refers to, to confirm a command,
   key, version or path.
5. MAINT-04 and MAINT-05 judge only the source files in this subject's list. Add
   `scope: <N> reviewed source files, not repo-wide` to `notes`. With no source files, mark both N/A
   ("no source files in scope").
6. Ownership: MAINT-02 judges repository-level layout and naming only (code-level cohesion, layering and cycles belong
   to `review-software-quality`). MAINT-05 judges reachable superseded code only (dead or commented-out code belongs to
   `review-software-quality` SQ-08). MR-15 judges placeholders only (real secrets belong to the security skills).
   Doc comments on public APIs belong to `review-software-quality` CS-04. License files and codes of conduct are
   judged here (MAINT-10; never a license-compatibility verdict on dependencies, which no subject judges since DEP-06
   was retired); `SECURITY.md` belongs to `review-software-lifecycle`.
7. Severity: every Finding takes the check's default severity from `checklist.md`; `checkResults.severityIfFailed`
   is always that default.
8. Citations: set `element` to the failed element's ID (e.g. `MR-14`); the report script derives `standard` and `url`
   from it, so don't write them. Give each distinct element violation its own finding.

#### Output

Findings, strengths and check results per `compliance-review-core`'s `finding-schema.md`.

### Checklist — Maintainability

Subject: Maintainability

| id | Sub-subject | Check | Default severity | Elements | Source |
|----|-------------|-------|------------------|----------|--------|
| MAINT-01 | README & Onboarding | A README states the project's purpose and documents setup, run and test instructions | Warning | MR-01–MR-06 | MR |
| MAINT-02 | Repository Layout | Repository layout and module boundaries are clear, consistent and match any documented structure | Information | MR-07–MR-12 | MR |
| MAINT-03 | Prerequisites & Configuration | Prerequisites, toolchain versions, environment variables/config keys and local dependencies are documented | Warning | MR-13–MR-16 | MR |
| MAINT-04 | Technical Debt | Technical-debt markers and warning suppressions in the reviewed files are tracked and justified, not piling up | Information | MR-17–MR-19 | MR |
| MAINT-05 | Deprecated Code | Superseded code in the reviewed files is marked deprecated with a replacement and removal target, and isn't still used silently | Information | MR-20–MR-23 | MR |
| MAINT-06 | Contributing Guide | A contributing guide explains the development workflow, pre-submit checks and conventions | Information | MR-24–MR-26 | MR |
| MAINT-07 | Change History | Change history is recorded per version and matches the published version | Information | MR-27–MR-29 | MR |
| MAINT-08 | Architecture Docs | Architecture and significant decisions are documented in editable form | Information | MR-30–MR-32 | MR |
| MAINT-09 | Docs Accuracy | Documentation matches the code: commands, keys, versions, paths and links are current | Warning | MR-33–MR-36 | MR |
| MAINT-10 | License & Conduct | The repository states its license (`LICENSE`/`LICENSE.md` or a manifest license field), consistently; public or open-source repos also have a code of conduct | Information | MR-37–MR-39 | MR |

Source key: MR = Compliance Reviewer Maintainability Rubric (`standards/maintainability-rubric.md`).

## File: `references/standards/maintainability-rubric.md`

*Load rule: MR-01…MR-36. Always load.*

### Compliance Reviewer Maintainability Rubric — local standard

- Level: every element is `REVIEW`; severity always comes from the owning check (SKILL.md).
- "Docs" means README, CONTRIBUTING, CHANGELOG, the `docs/` folder and ADRs in the subject's file list.
- A debt marker is *tracked* when it has an issue key, an issue URL, or an owner plus a date.

| ID | Level | Requirement | Applies when | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MR-01 | REVIEW | A root README exists and its opening section states what the project is and does. | always (evidence rule for "missing") | MAINT-01 |
| MR-02 | REVIEW | README (or a doc it links) gives setup or install steps that work from a clean checkout. | README exists | MAINT-01 |
| MR-03 | REVIEW | README gives the command(s) to build and run the application or library locally. | README exists | MAINT-01 |
| MR-04 | REVIEW | README gives the command(s) to run the automated tests. | README exists and test code or a test config is in the listing | MAINT-01 |
| MR-05 | REVIEW | Commands are copy-pasteable: in fenced code blocks, with any placeholders explained. | README has commands | MAINT-01 |
| MR-06 | REVIEW | README links to the deeper docs that exist (docs folder, CONTRIBUTING, architecture, CHANGELOG). | such docs exist in the listing | MAINT-01 |
| MR-07 | REVIEW | The top-level layout follows one recognizable convention for the stack (e.g. `src/` + `tests/`, one project per folder) and applies it consistently. | folder listing in scope | MAINT-02 |
| MR-08 | REVIEW | Folder, project and module names state their responsibility; no catch-all folders (`misc`, `stuff`, `temp`, `new`, `old`) hold production code. | folder listing in scope | MAINT-02 |
| MR-09 | REVIEW | Test code is kept apart from production code (separate folder or project, or one consistent naming pattern). | test code present | MAINT-02 |
| MR-10 | REVIEW | Where docs describe the intended structure, the actual layout matches it. | docs describe the structure | MAINT-02 |
| MR-11 | REVIEW | Build output, caches and generated code (`bin/`, `obj/`, `dist/`, `node_modules/`, `__pycache__/`) aren't committed, or generated code is marked and kept separate. | folder listing in scope | MAINT-02 |
| MR-12 | REVIEW | A multi-module repository has a root-level map of its modules (solution or workspace file, or a README section). | more than one module, project or deployable | MAINT-02 |
| MR-13 | REVIEW | Required tools and versions (runtime/SDK, package manager, database, container engine) are stated in docs or pinned (`global.json`, `.nvmrc`, `.python-version`, `.tool-versions`, `rust-toolchain*`). | always | MAINT-03 |
| MR-14 | REVIEW | Every env var or config key the reviewed files read is documented with purpose and example, or listed in a template (`.env.example`, sample settings). | the reviewed files read env vars or config keys | MAINT-03 |
| MR-15 | REVIEW | Secrets are documented by name and where to get them only; templates and samples hold placeholders, not real-looking values. | a template or sample config exists | MAINT-03 |
| MR-16 | REVIEW | External services needed to run locally (database, queue, cache, cloud emulator) have setup steps or a local stack (`docker-compose*`, dev container). | the app depends on external services | MAINT-03 |
| MR-17 | REVIEW | `TODO`/`FIXME`/`HACK`/`XXX` markers carry a tracking reference: issue key or URL, or owner plus date. | markers present in reviewed source files | MAINT-04 |
| MR-18 | REVIEW | Untracked markers don't pile up: fewer than 3 per reviewed file, and no untracked `FIXME`/`HACK` in error-handling, security or data-access code. | markers present in reviewed source files | MAINT-04 |
| MR-19 | REVIEW | Suppressed warnings (`#pragma warning disable`, `[SuppressMessage]`, `@SuppressWarnings`, `eslint-disable`, `# noqa`, `# type: ignore`) give a reason next to them. | suppressions present in reviewed source files | MAINT-04 |
| MR-20 | REVIEW | Deprecated APIs use the language mechanism (`[Obsolete]`, `@Deprecated`, `DeprecationWarning` / `@deprecated`, JSDoc `@deprecated`) with a message naming the replacement. | deprecated or legacy code in reviewed files | MAINT-05 |
| MR-21 | REVIEW | Each deprecation states a removal target (version or date) or a tracking reference. | deprecation markers present | MAINT-05 |
| MR-22 | REVIEW | Code marked deprecated isn't still called from other reviewed non-test code without a justified suppression. | deprecation markers present | MAINT-05 |
| MR-23 | REVIEW | Superseded copies kept side by side (`FooOld`, `LegacyBar`, `v1/` next to `v2/`) carry a deprecation marker or retirement plan. Unreachable or commented-out code is SQ-08. | legacy-named or versioned copies in reviewed files or the listing | MAINT-05 |
| MR-24 | REVIEW | A CONTRIBUTING guide (or a README section) explains the workflow: branching, pull requests and review expectations. | always (evidence rule for "missing") | MAINT-06 |
| MR-25 | REVIEW | It says how to run formatters, linters and tests before submitting, and the commands match the tooling config in the repo. | guide exists | MAINT-06 |
| MR-26 | REVIEW | It states the coding conventions or points to the enforced config (`.editorconfig`, linter or formatter config). | guide exists | MAINT-06 |
| MR-27 | REVIEW | A CHANGELOG or release-notes file exists, or the README links to release notes. | repo publishes versioned artifacts (publishable manifest name + version, release pipeline, or versioned API) | MAINT-07 |
| MR-28 | REVIEW | Entries are grouped by version with a date, and call out breaking changes and deprecations. | change log exists | MAINT-07 |
| MR-29 | REVIEW | The latest version in the change log matches the version in the manifest in scope. | change log and manifest both in scope | MAINT-07 |
| MR-30 | REVIEW | An architecture overview names the main components, what each is responsible for and how they interact (text or diagram). | more than one module, project or deployable, or a layered structure | MAINT-08 |
| MR-31 | REVIEW | Significant decisions are recorded (ADRs or a decisions section) with context and consequences. | same as MR-30 | MAINT-08 |
| MR-32 | REVIEW | Diagrams are kept in an editable source form (Mermaid, PlantUML, draw.io, Structurizr), not only as images. | diagrams present | MAINT-08 |
| MR-33 | REVIEW | Commands, scripts and paths named in docs exist (e.g. a documented `npm run test` is defined in `package.json`; a referenced folder is in the listing). | docs name commands, scripts or paths | MAINT-09 |
| MR-34 | REVIEW | Env vars and config keys named in docs still exist in the templates or reviewed code (no stale entries). Missing documentation is MR-14. | docs name env vars or keys | MAINT-09 |
| MR-35 | REVIEW | Versions stated in docs (runtime, SDK, framework) match the manifests or toolchain pins in scope. | docs state versions and a manifest or pin is in scope | MAINT-09 |
| MR-36 | REVIEW | Relative links in docs point to files and anchors that exist. | docs contain relative links | MAINT-09 |
| MR-37 | REVIEW | The repository states its license: a `LICENSE`/`LICENSE.md`/`COPYING` file at the root, or a license field in the root package manifest (`license` in `package.json`/`pyproject.toml`, `<licenses>` in `pom.xml`, `PackageLicenseExpression` in a `*.csproj`). | always (root listing in scope) | MAINT-10 |
| MR-38 | REVIEW | A license stated in more than one place is consistent (the license file and the manifest field name the same license). | license file and manifest field both in scope | MAINT-10 |
| MR-39 | REVIEW | Public or open-source repositories have a code of conduct (`CODE_OF_CONDUCT*` at the root, in `.github/` or in `docs/`), or the README or CONTRIBUTING links one. | the repo is public or open source (an OSI license, a public package manifest or a public forge URL in the files) | MAINT-10 |
